lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: common probabilistic reasoning errors

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.

items.prompt: A box holds 16 items, of which 3 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Given P(A and B) = 1/20 and P(B) = 6/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 31/100, P(B) = 35/100, and P(A and B) = 11/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.
The two events are mutually exclusive.

items.prompt: A box holds 6 items, of which 2 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 25/100 and P(B) = 29/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 22/100, P(B) = 15/100, and P(A and B) = 12/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: In a study, the probability of a delay is the same whether or not it is raining. What is the correct interpretation?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A box holds 19 items, of which 7 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
